second_order: Mobilizing Canadians to build and expand canvas symbols
theme_note: These codes turn flags, words, animals, provincial emblems, and successor-canvas ideas into calls for pixel labour. What varies is the object and scale: starting a flag, enlarging it, adding an anthem or emblem, or recruiting for another Canadian mark.

These codes make broad ambitions workable through coordinates, grids, templates, proportions, reference images, navigation links, and line-by-line instructions. What varies is whether participants are locating work, choosing a design, or resolving a local pixel constraint.

second_order: Keeping shared images up through repair and defence
theme_note: These codes describe the recurring labour of restoring colours, cleaning letters, guarding borders, answering attacks, and maintaining completed-looking work. What varies is the threat and method, from manual five-minute pixels and night watches to proposed scripts and appeals for backup.

second_order: Joking through pixel work and its mistakes
theme_note: These codes use jokes to sustain participation and reinterpret awkward designs, grammar detours, altered words, weed leaves, and the final 158. What varies is whether humour recruits, teases, excuses damage, or turns a frozen mistake into a shared story.

second_order: Negotiating and fighting over canvas space
theme_note: These codes manage relations with neighbouring images and communities through borders, coexistence, aid, alliances, truces, invasions, overwriting, apologies, and refusals. What varies is whether participants seek restraint and reciprocity or treat the same shared space as a target.

second_order: Claiming, judging, and remembering the result
theme_note: These codes assess what the room made: reporting progress, calling a flag shameful or perfect, celebrating contribution, preserving snapshots, assigning credit, declaring success or failure, and explaining the final image. What varies is timing and stance, from live appraisal to post-close retrospection.

second_order: Running April Fools bait and unpacking it
theme_note: These non-canvas codes stage implausible Canadian rail and bridge claims, expose or extend the bait, and turn it into practical discussion. What varies is whether commenters keep the prank going, correct it, or use it to discuss transport and access.

second_order: Arguing Canada and Quebec through the canvas
theme_note: These codes use Canadian and Quebec flags to dispute equal space, preservation, destruction, language, history, and shared national belonging. What varies is whether Quebec is treated as a neighbour to protect, territory to absorb, or a standpoint from which Canadian unity is challenged.

These codes move or contain event discussion through stickies, r/placecanada, Discord, existing threads, removals, and rule explanations, while participants challenge or work around those decisions. What varies is who initiates the move and whether it is accepted, resisted, or used to circulate plans back.
